w: Swamishri visited the Mayor's office in downtown Houston at the City Hall. Mayor Lee Brown cordially welcomed Swamishri. The Mayor was happy to learn of Swamishri's socio-spiritual activities and efforts for peace and harmony. He honored Swamishri by presenting the Key to the City and a certificate of Honorary Citizen and Goodwill Ambassador of the city of Houston.

At 6.25 p.m. Swamishri arrived at the Swaminarayan Mandir in Ramol and performed pujan, arti and mantra pushpanjali of the murtis. After blessing the Satsang assembly Swamishri stopped over for darshan at the Swaminarayan mandir in Kaloli and then proceeded.

A devotee revealed his problem to Swamishri, “My wife and I have two different approaches to raising our child. Whenever our child becomes rowdy and mischievous I lovingly try to explain and correct him. But my wife hits and scolds him. Consequently there is a difference of opinion between us. What should I do?” Swamishri advised, “A child is ignorant and unaware of the disturbances he causes. It is important to talk to him and make him understand with love. If you treat him with love then he will change and progress. By hitting him he will never advance in life. Hence make him understand and try to correct him with love.”

The husband of Mayoress Becky Miller of Carollton City and the husband of State Representative Linda Harper-Brown, Mr Leel Brown, presented a proclamation and Key to the City to Swamishri. In the evening assembly balaks and kishores presented a programme on Swamishri’s tremendous efforts in developing Satsang in USA through his vicharans from 1977 onwards. The presentation was interspersed with dramas and speeches of veteran devotees. Thereafter the Mayoress and State Representative were honoured by the women volunteers and their husbands were honoured and blessed by Swamishri. Both the honoured guests were also the chief guests of the women’s convention held in the afternoon. Finally, Swamishri blessed the assembly lauding the evening programme and the faith, understanding, sacrifice and unity of the devotees who endeavoured in spreading Satsang.

2 September (V.S. 2063, Shravan vad 6) Sunday, Dallas At 11.20 am Swamishri performed the murti-pratishtha rituals of pujan and arti of the marble murtis of Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj, Radha-Krishna Dev, Sita-Ram and Hanumanji, Shiv-Parvati and Ganpatiji, Nilkanth Varni (abhishek murti) and the Guru Parampara. The murtis would be established in the two new hari mandirs in Dallas (presently under construction) and Lubbock town. The Governor of Texas, Rick Perry, had sent a welcoming letter to Swamishri. Swamishri blessed Congressman Pete Sessions and Congressman Kenny Marchant, who presented a welcoming letter to Swamishri. The Mayor of Irving City, Herbert Gears, presented a proclamation to Swamishri. After their addresses Swamishri was honoured with garlands by senior sadhus. Thereafter the kishores and yuvaks performed a cultural dance to celebrate the mandir pratishtha festival. Finally, Swamishri blessed the assembly by elaborating about the restlessness of the mind. He added that to stabilize it one has to understand and imbibe the glory of God. Later, Swamishri consecrated an abhishek murti of Shri Nilkanth Varni in the present hari mandir. The next day Swamishri departed from Dallas at 5.30 pm and landed at San Jose International airport at (9.20 pm, Dallas time) 7.20 pm San Jose time.
3 to 8 September 2007, San Jose During Swamishri’s stay volunteer devotees from San Francisco, Sacramento and Fresno gave reports on their respective satsang activities.

st.t: Symbolic Festival Celebrations - Navratri, Diwali & Annakut in Swamishri’s Presence
w: Since Swamishri’s arrival in Amdavad on 1 September 2008, he had blessed the sadhus and devotees with divine joy. The last day of his stay was marked with the celebrations of three festivals: Annakut, Diwali and Navratri.

Over 350 varieties of vegetarian delicacies were devoutly offered to Thakorji in the form of a grand Annakut. Before his morning puja Swamishri performed the Annakut arti and blessed that such devotion continues to flourish in everyone’s hearts.
During Swamishri’s morning puja, the sadhus sang bhajans in commemoration of Diwali. Swamishri’s serene murti was the focal point of attention as youths in special diva costumes lit the stage.
Finally, after his puja, Swamishri heralded the first day of the annual Navratri festival by joyfully playing with the ras sticks as the sadhus sang a traditional dance bhajan.

Today a blood test was to be done to keep watch over Pramukh Swami Maharaj's health. After his puja, Swamishri came to the meeting room. Here a doctor was making preparations to take Swamishri's blood. Many sadhus were standing around. Because of this, the doctor seemed a little nervous. Swamishri understood this, so he said laughingly, "Take whatever blood you want, while worshipping the beloved Swami." In this way Swamishri lightened the atmosphere. So the doctor too was put at ease.

That Swamishri understands people's minds became clear only at night, when Swamishri got up from his chair before retiring. At that time, revealing the secret of the morning, Swamishri said, "The doctor was getting ready. In front of him were Bapu and the sadhus. So I made up that song, 'Take whatever blood you want, while worshipping the beloved Swami.'"
During the meetings, Becharbhai of Chakampar came. Seeing him, Pramukh Swami Maharaj said, "Now you have become very old."

In 1957, when Swamishri was in Rohishala with Sant Swami, he had accepted this Becharbhai's request and, in the pouring rain, wading through the mud, walked from Rohishala to Chakampar for a padharamani. Swamishri had kept up his acquaintance with him ever since that time.

Pramukh Swami Maharaj was having his evening meal. Among the sadhus sitting in front, Swamishri said to Tyagraj Swami, who looks after the city's satsang activities here, "Does that Nanabhai come every day?"
Nanabhai is an old Khoja devotee of Bhavnagar. He has great affection for Swamishri. Since the time of Shastriji Maharaj, Swamishri has had a loving relationship with the Khoja families here.
Viveksagar Swami said, "He comes every day. He even sent word to me, 'Tell Swami Bapa that I come to the katha every day.'"

Hearing this, Swamishri said to Tyagraj Swami, "Bring Nanabhai tomorrow." Having said this, he added with a sweet rebuke, "You live right here. Do you not know that the old devotees should be brought?!"
Tyagraj Swami said, "He was left out on the day we arranged the meeting for the old devotees."
Swamishri said, "What do you mean, left out? You should know. No one should be left out."
In this way, Swamishri made sure that such care was kept.

To keep a check on Pramukh Swami Maharaj's health, a blood test was to be done today. After his puja, Swamishri came to the meeting room. Here a doctor was getting ready to take Swamishri's blood. Many sants were standing around. Because of this the doctor seemed a little nervous. Swamishri understood this, so smiling he said, "Take whatever blood you wish to take, as I worship my beloved Swami." In this way Swamishri lightened the atmosphere. So the doctor too was relieved.

That Swamishri understands people's minds became clear only at night, when Swamishri got up from his chair before going to sleep. Explaining the secret of the morning, Swamishri said, "The doctor was getting ready. Bapu and the sants were in front of him. So I made up that song, 'Take whatever blood you wish to take, as I worship my beloved Swami.'"
During the meetings, Becharbhai of Chakampar came. Seeing him, Pramukh Swami Maharaj said, "Now you have become very old."

In 1957, when Swamishri was in Rohishala with Sant Swami, he accepted this Becharbhai's request and, in pouring rain, walked from Rohishala to Chakampar through the mud for a padhramani. Swamishri had kept his acquaintance with him alive ever since that incident.

Pramukh Swami Maharaj was having his evening meal. Of the sants sitting in front, Swamishri said to Tyagraj Swami, who looks after the city satsang activities here, "Does that Nanabhai come every day?"
Nanabhai is an old Khoja devotee of Bhavnagar. He has great affection for Swamishri. Since the time of Shastriji Maharaj, Swamishri has had a loving bond with the Khoja families here.
Viveksagar Swami said, "He comes every day. He even sent word to me, 'Tell Swami Bapa that I come to the katha every day.'"

Hearing this, Swamishri said to Tyagraj Swami, "Bring Nanabhai tomorrow." Having said this, with a sweet rebuke he said, "You live right here, don't you know that the old devotees should be brought?!"
Tyagraj Swami said, "The other day, when we arranged for the old devotees, he was left out."
Swamishri said, "How was he left out? You should know, no one should be left out."
In this way, Swamishri made them mindful.
As yesterday, Mahant Swami Maharaj cut short his rest and came to a session of the North America Leadership Seminar.
In the session, Swamishri was asked, "How can groupism be removed?"

Swamishri said, "How much inspiration this body gives us! In the body, the lungs, liver, kidneys and all the organs each do their own work in harmony with one another, but they do not form groups. If they did, it would be the end of the person. They are all together, and they nourish one another. They do each other's work. If we make unity into one body, there will be no conflict."
Today, in the evening assembly, Mahant Swami Maharaj said in his blessings:

"We studied in KG (kindergarten): 'He that is down needs fear no fall...' (he recited the whole poem). A person's satsang is judged by seeing his servanthood. Cloth is measured in metres, water in litres. In the same way, a person's satsang is measured by servanthood and love for Bhagwan; it is directly proportional. There is great joy in servanthood. You owe nothing to anyone. No one gets in your way. It is the best of all qualities."

st.t: ‘A Tour to Remember’: Australian Chief Minister Visits Swaminarayan Akshardham in Delhi
w: Chief Minister of the Australian Capital Territory Andrew Barr visited Swaminarayan Akshardham in New Delhi, along with a delegation of Australian government and university officials, as part of a trip to India meant to encourage more Indian visitors to Australia.
The delegation was traditionally greeted by senior swamijis on behalf of Param Pujya Mahant Swami Maharaj, the current spiritual leader of BAPS.

During the Chief Minister’s visit, he offered respects at the Swaminarayan Akshardham Mandir and performed abhishek, the ceremonial pouring of sanctified water from 151 holy bodies of water from across India on the murti of Shri Neelkanth Varni. The group also toured the educational Sanskruti Vihar, a cultural voyage that displays 10,000 years of India’s heritage and contributions to society and saw the Neelkanth Darshan – a Giant Screen film on the epic journey of Neelkanth Varni throughout India. Finally, they witnessed the Sahaj Anand Water Show.
At the conclusion of his visit, Barr said Akshardham was a “tour to remember.”
